meta.workDescription: As a fire department, we have many training and real world incident responsibilities that provide various risks to our personnel on a daily basis.

selectedModules.title: Hazardous Energy Control
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 21; 29 CFR 1910.147 - The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train authorized employees on hazardous energy sources, magnitude, and isolation methods; affected employees on the purpose and use of procedures; and other nearby employees on restart/reenergization prohibitions. Retrain when assignments, equipment, processes, or procedures change, or when inspections show gaps.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.147 - The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: DAFMAN 91-203 establishes a formal Hazardous Energy Control Program with dedicated training, documented procedures, and periodic self-inspections before servicing or maintenance work is performed.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 21

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.reference: AFI 90-821 - Hazard Communication (HAZCOM) Program; 29 CFR 1910.1200 - Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide effective training at initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced. Cover where hazardous chemicals are present, the written program, labels and SDS access, how releases are detected, hazard types, protective measures, emergency procedures, and required PPE.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.1200 - Hazard Communication
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Employees potentially exposed to chemical hazards must complete HAZCOM training upon initial assignment and whenever a new hazard or chemical is introduced or new tasks create new hazards. Supervisors must ensure SDS access for chemicals used in the work process.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 28.2.5 and para. 28.3.3

selectedModules.title: Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.reference: 29 CFR 1910.1030 - Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train exposed employees at initial assignment and at least annually, with additional training when tasks or procedures create new exposure. Cover disease signs and transmission, the exposure control plan, task recognition, engineering controls, work practices, PPE use and disposal, and Hepatitis B vaccine information.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.1030 - Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Any person whose duties involve reasonably anticipated exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material must be trained and enrolled in the Bloodborne Pathogen Program. Supervisors of affected workplaces must establish a written exposure control plan and conduct training.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 1.9

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.reference: AFI 48-127 - Occupational Noise and Hearing Conservation Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide a hearing conservation training program for employees exposed at or above the action level, repeat it annually, and update it when equipment or work processes change. Cover hearing effects, protector selection and care, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.95 - Occupational noise exposure
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Hazardous noise concerns must be evaluated and controls recommended through the occupational health risk assessment process. Use the AF Hearing Conservation Program as the training and control basis when shop noise hazards are identified.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 2.2.2

selectedModules.title: Confined Space Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 23; 29 CFR 1910.146 - Permit-required confined spaces
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train affected employees before first assignment, before duty changes, when permit-space operations introduce new hazards, and when deviations or inadequate knowledge are identified. Training must establish proficiency and be documented by employee, trainer, and date.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.146 - Permit-required confined spaces
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Employees entering confined spaces must be trained to safely accomplish assigned duties and rescue procedures for the specific permit-required space entered. Safety observers and attendants must also be trained on rescue procedures for each type of permit-required confined space.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 28.2.9 and para. 28.3.2

selectedModules.title: Respiratory Protection Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 48-137 - Respiratory Protection Program; AF Form 2767 - Occupational Health Training & Protective Equipment Fit Testing
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide comprehensive, understandable respirator training before use and at least annually thereafter. Cover why the respirator is needed, limitations, emergency use, inspection, donning and seal checks, maintenance and storage, and symptoms that may limit safe use.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.134 - Respiratory protection
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Respiratory hazards must be evaluated by Bioenvironmental Engineering and respiratory protection used where required by the occupational health assessment. Use the AF Respiratory Protection Program for controls, fit testing, and local training requirements.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 2.2.4 and para. 28.2.11

selectedModules.title: Fall Arrest Systems
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 13; 29 CFR 1910.66 - Powered platforms for building maintenance; 29 CFR 1926.503 - Training requirements
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel in safe personal fall arrest system use before use and after any component or system change. Pair this with the AF and local fall protection requirements for inspection, anchorage, rescue, and user limitations.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.66 - Powered platforms for building maintenance
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Any work above four feet requires a fall protection program and appropriate safety gear. Use the local fall protection program, rescue procedures, and chapter-specific AF requirements for application-level training.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 28.2.7 and Chapter 13

selectedModules.title: Explosives Safety Training
selectedModules.reference: DESR 6055.09_DAFMAN 91-201 - Explosives Safety Standards; DAFI 91-202 - The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Mishap Prevention Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use explosives-specific AF lesson plans and local operating instructions. OSHA 2254 includes transportation and explosives references, but the Air Force explosives program should remain the primary training basis for this module.
selectedModules.trainingSource: DESR 6055.09_DAFMAN 91-201 - Explosives Safety Standards / local procedures

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Where work conditions require trained first-aid responders, ensure personnel are adequately trained and available. OSHA 2254 links first-aid and CPR availability to certain work settings, but local mission risk and AF requirements should define who must hold current CPR credentials.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.151 - Medical services and first aid and 1910.269; DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Initial first aid and CPR training must be completed before assigning duties that require it, refresher training must occur before certification expires, and CPR training must include PAD instruction. Remote or high-risk work must have an immediate medical response plan.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 1.8

selectedModules.title: Flight Line Driving
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 24
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use flight-line-specific AF lesson plans and local airfield driving rules. OSHA 2254 does not provide a direct flight-line driving training excerpt for this module.
selectedModules.trainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards / local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use Chapter 24 flightline vehicle operations rules and local licensing programs. For specialized equipment like forklifts and hi-lifts around aircraft, only licensed drivers may operate and the owning organization must provide special training with spotter support as required.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 24.13 and para. 24.13.10

selectedModules.title: Medical Surveillance Examination
selectedModules.reference: DAFI 48-145 - Occupational and Environmental Health Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Tie this module to the specific exposure program and explain when surveillance is required, how scheduling works, and what triggers follow-up. OSHA 2254 aligns most directly where laboratory or substance-specific standards require information on exposure limits, signs and symptoms, and protective measures, but the AF medical surveillance program should remain the primary driver.
selectedModules.trainingSource: Partial OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards alignment with 29 CFR 1910.1450 - Occupational exposure to hazardous chemicals in laboratories and exposure-specific standards
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the occupational health risk assessment and exposure-specific program requirements to decide who needs surveillance, what triggers enrollment, and what training or briefings must accompany the surveillance requirement.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 2.2 and DAFI 48-145 - Occupational and Environmental Health Program

selectedModules.title: Laser Safety Training
selectedModules.reference: AFI 48-139 - Laser and Optical Radiation Protection Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use AF laser program guidance for laser classes, beam hazards, eyewear selection, alignment controls, and access restrictions. No direct OSHA 2254 module is mapped here.
selectedModules.trainingSource: AFI 48-139 - Laser and Optical Radiation Protection Program

selectedModules.title: Ladder Safety
selectedModules.reference: Common local training item often broken out separately with fixed and portable ladder rules
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use local ladder lesson plans, manufacturer instructions, and AF walking-working surface guidance. OSHA 2254 (2015 edition) does not provide a dedicated general-industry ladder training summary in the same way it does for lockout, forklifts, or confined spaces, so this remains primarily AF/local-driven.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Personnel using ladders at any working height must be trained when first assigned, and that training must include hands-on instruction covering ladder defects, electrocution hazards, positioning, and placement for various job sites. Training must be documented under DAFI 91-202.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 7.4.3.7

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Local emergency response briefing and lockdown procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Tie this to the local emergency action plan, shelter/lockdown locations, notification methods, and commander-directed response procedures.
selectedModules.trainingSource: Local emergency action plan

selectedModules.title: Government Vehicle / Utility Vehicle Use
selectedModules.reference: Local GOV, GVO, or UTV operating rules and licensing expectations
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Document local licensing, route restrictions, spotter use, rollover protection, and unit-specific operating rules. OSHA 2254 does not provide a direct GOV/UTV training excerpt here.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: Manual lifting techniques and available lifting devices
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Cover shop-specific lifting limits, two-person lift triggers, hand truck and lifting-device use, and when supervisors require assisted handling. No direct OSHA 2254 standalone manual-lifting module is mapped here.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Supervisors must ensure thorough training on proper manual lifting techniques, required PPE, and the use of manual lifting devices. Training must use both verbal and written materials, include practice on proper motions, and be documented under DAFI 91-202.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 2.10.3

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: Local extinguisher, pull station, and fire reporting procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Review the fire prevention plan with employees when the plan is developed, when responsibilities change, and when the plan changes. If extinguishers are provided for employee use, train employees on the general principles of extinguisher use and the hazards of incipient-stage firefighting at initial assignment and at least annually. Train designated users on the specific equipment they are expected to use.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.39 - Fire prevention plans and 1910.157
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Facility managers and supervisors must establish and maintain a fire prevention training program through the JSTO so employees understand their fire prevention and protection responsibilities in their work areas. This is fulfilled through job safety training and documentation under DAFI 91-202.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 6.2.1.1

selectedModules.title: Thermal Stress / Heat and Cold Stress
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; DAFI 48-145 - Occupational and Environmental Health Program; local Bioenvironmental Engineering or Occupational Health guidance
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Cover heat stress, cold stress, WBGT or locally directed exposure monitoring, acclimatization, hydration, work/rest cycles, buddy checks, PPE or clothing considerations, symptom recognition, supervisor notification, and emergency response actions for suspected heat illness or cold injury.
selectedModules.trainingSource: AF occupational safety and occupational health guidance; local BE/OEH procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the occupational health risk assessment, local BE recommendations, and supervisor hazard controls to brief personnel on thermal stress hazards and controls for hot, cold, humid, outdoor, flight line, industrial, or PPE-intensive work areas.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards and DAFI 48-145 - Occupational and Environmental Health Program

selectedModules.title: Ergonomics / Office and Administrative Workstation Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; OSHA ergonomics guidance; local Bioenvironmental Engineering or Occupational Health guidance
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Cover workstation setup, chair adjustment, monitor height and distance, keyboard and mouse position, neutral posture, repetitive motion, micro-pauses or task variation, safe lifting of office supplies, file cabinet and storage safety, early reporting of discomfort, and how to request a BE ergonomic assessment when needed.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA ergonomics guidance; local BE/OEH procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use DAFMAN 91-203 office safety and ergonomics guidance to brief administrative and computer-based workers on musculoskeletal disorder risk factors, workstation adjustment, posture, repetitive motion controls, manual handling of office materials, and supervisor follow-up for ergonomic concerns.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 2

selectedModules.title: Jewelry / Loose Articles Restrictions
selectedModules.reference: Workplace-specific limits on rings, necklaces, watches, and loose items
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use local shop rules and hazard analysis to define where jewelry, loose clothing, or unsecured items are prohibited around moving parts, climbing, electrical work, or snag hazards.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
